# Releasing Osaurus

Super messy notes for the new guy...

- 2 products: 1.x and Classic. Decide which one by the tag version.
- 1.x: `main` branch, tags `1.Y.Z`, `1.Y.Z-beta.N`
- Classic: `classic` branch, tags `0.25.N`
- `release_lane.py` auto decides for you at every step

|  | Osaurus 1.x | Osaurus Classic 0.25.x |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Branch | `main` | `classic` |
| Tags | `1.Y.Z`, `1.Y.Z-beta.N` | `0.25.N` |
| Sparkle feed | `docs/appcast-next.xml` | `docs/appcast.xml` |
| GitHub Latest, website, Homebrew | Stable releases | Never |
| Model-bundled DMG | Yes | No |
| Release notes | Auto draft from `main` | Hand-written |

Classic only gets fixes. New stuff goes to `main`. PRs to `classic` start with `Classic:`

Release Drafter updates the newest draft on `main` pushes. 1.x notes: just overwrite or restore after last merge before tagging.

## Releasing 1.x

1. Merge to `main`.
2. Wait for CI green: `test-core`, `test-cli`, `swiftlint`, `shellcheck`. No CI, no go.
3. Review the auto-draft.
4. Tag it: `git tag 1.0.1 && git push origin 1.0.1`.

Stable 1.x also updates Classic upgrade offer. Beta skip this.

## Releasing Classic patch

1. Branch from `classic`, fix, & PR. Title starts `Classic:`.
2. Wait for green CI.
3. Draft release with notes. Pipeline needs this for Classic. Notes start with "Classic maintenance".
4. Tag it: `0.25.N`.

### Never

- Never mix 0.x and 1.x tags. Wrong tag ships 1.0 to Classic users. Both tag attempts fail.
- Never edit `appcast.xml` or `next.xml` by hand. Pipeline writes them.
- Never mark Classic as Latest. 1.x must be the Latest for GitHub, website, Homebrew. Full DMG lives in `OsaurusAI/osaurus-releases`. Only relabeled for Latest releases (never beta or Classic).

## Classic upgrade offer

Stable 1.x adds its item to `appcast.xml` beta channel. Classic asks only when **Beta Updates** is on in Settings → General. Offers 1.0 update with `minimumAutoupdateVersion` 1.0.0. Only one 1.x item allowed in `appcast.xml` beta.

## End of Classic support

Move all Classic to 1.x by publishing 1.x to `appcast.xml` release channel. `release_lane.py` needs a change for this. After, freeze `classic`.

---

Hope this helps, new guy! Good luck! 🤞

Hey there, new colleague! 😄 Here's how to do the Sourcery release thingy. Super important to check out this link first: https://github.com/krzysztofzablocki/Sourcery/issues/1247#issuecomment-1892571851 - it’s the step-by-step deal.

So, no strict rules on when to do releases. Bug fixes: do 'em often. New features: less often. Breaking API changes: rare as heck. 🙅‍♂️

For versioning, follow SemVer:
- Patch version (3rd number): bug fixes and tiny changes (eg., 0.6.0 -> 0.6.1).
- Minor version (2nd number): big new stuff or breaking changes (eg., 0.6.1 -> 0.7.0).

Need to be an owner for CocoaPods Trunk and have access to the Sourcery repo.

Install brew if you need to update the Homebrew formula.

Now, for the release itself, we're using rake. Say, you want to release `0.6.1`. Here's what happens:
1. Installs stuff (Bundler, CocoaPods).
2. Checks if docs are fresh.
3. CI checks if master is green.
4. Updates internal boilerplate code.
5. Runs tests.
6. Asks for the new version and updates metadata.
7. Creates a new GitHub release.
8. Pushes to CocoaPods Trunk.
9. Pushes to Homebrew (you'll need to input your username and password manually for a PR).
10. Prepares for the next dev cycle.

Be careful with auto-changes and make sure you approve them. 🧐

OK, so here’s the deal, buddy:

- First things first, go to Beads and make sure every child of the release epic is closed or dropped. Super important.
- Look at the comments and doc changes since the last release. You'll want to skim this to make sure nothing's off. 📝
- Kick off the build on `develop`. Make sure the full test suite and `swift format lint...` pass. No skips here!

Quick note: you're gonna want to snap a code health photo. 📸 Don’t forget that.

- Now, bump that app version in `Mochi Diffusion.xcodeproj/project.xcproj`. Only do this once in the commit. 📝
- Add a changelog entry for the upcoming version top of `CHANGELOG.md`. And date it for when you're releasing it.
- Also, check out the new or changed localizable strings. Merging to `main` fires off a Crowdin upload for translations.

Alright, so you’re doing all this on a release branch `release- `, cut from `develop`. 👍

**Tools you'll need:**
- Xcode, signed in with the Developer ID team.
- `create-dmg` from npm (`npm install --global create-dmg`).
- `sign_update` and `generate_keys` from the `bin` folder of a Sparkle release.

Side note: Don't put any secrets in the repo, release notes, or in a shell command. 🔐

- Store notarization creds under the profile name the notarize step uses. 🗝️
- Import the Sparkle private key (keep it in the keychain and delete the file after importing). Remember to back it up in a password manager. Losing this key = no more updates for installed users.

**Release Steps:**
1. Merge the release branch into `main` via a pull request:
   - Push `release- ` and open a PR to `main`.
   - Wait for the Gated Check-in workflow to pass. If it fails, fix and push again.
   - Merge with Create a merge commit. Don't squash.
   - CI workflow on `main` should pass.
   - Fast-forward `develop` to `main`.

2. Build and notarize the app from `main`:
   - In Xcode, go to Product > Archive.
   - Use Organizer > Distribute App > Direct Distribution.
   - Export `Mochi Diffusion.app` once notarization is done.

3. Make the DMG in the export folder using `create-dmg`.

4. Notarize the DMG and staple the ticket.

5. Tag the release commit `v `. On GitHub, draft a release, attach the DMG, and publish.

6. Sign the DMG for Sparkle using `sign_update`.

7. Add a new version entry at the top of `.sparkle/appcast.xml` on `main`. Use the format of the previous item. Attributes needed include:
   - `sparkle:version`: the `CFBundleVersion` from the app.
   - `sparkle:shortVersion`: same as above.

Good luck, and don't mess this up! 😅

OK, so here's how you actually dive into ReSwift contributions:

- First, the style guide? It’s kinda strict but with one big exception: **use 4 spaces for indentation, not tabs**. That’s important! (Ray Wenderlich Style Guide... yeah, I know, but 4 spaces, got it?)

- SwiftLint: It runs on PRs, so if you have it installed, you'll see warnings in Xcode. Freq warning: function body lengths in tests. Use `// swiftlint:disable function_body_length` at the start of the func. Common issues: trailing whitespace and valid docs. 👍

- Tests: **NO test, no merge**. Aim for 100% coverage. It's all about those edge cases, especially nil conditions. Tests run in Travis CI, same as in Xcode.

- Comments: 
  - Aim for readable code over commented. Only use comments for non-obvious stuff, like why some code that looks unnecessary is actually needed.
  - Update or remove comments when the code changes. Outdated comments are worse than no comments at all.

- Code docs: More important than comments. You need to document everything well. Here's what matters:
  - Quick help in Xcode
  - API docs
  - Dash docsets
  - Current, all params & return types documented, common issues noted
  - Check NSHipster Swift for ref.

- Docs gen: The script `generate_docs.sh` processes Markdown files to generate final docs. Key files:
  - README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE.md
  - Docs/Getting Started Guide.md, Docs/templates/heading.md, toc.md
  - Docs/Actions.md, Reducers.md, State.md, Stores.md, Utilities.md

- Script: `generate_docs.sh` extracts sections, adds titles, replaces version tags, and does random replacements (check `.jazzy.json` under "string-replacements").

- Hosting: Docs are on GitHub pages under the gh-pages branch. The `build.sh` script in gh-pages branch: pulls latest master, runs `generate_docs.sh`, commits & pushes to gh-pages.

- Theme: Located in `Docs/jazzy-theme`.

- PRs: Open on master. If you're stuck on the rules, **still open the PR**. We'll help.

Got all that? Yeah, it’s a bit of a mess. Good luck! 🤞

Hey new guy, here’s how you jump into Kitura without drowning:

- First, you gotta get familiar with the coding standards, or Swift Lint will be cranky. 🤓

- **First-timer tip:** Look for the "good first issue" label. These are usually doc fixes, minor bug fixes, and refactoring tasks. Super handy for getting your feet wet.

- Fork the repo and clone it:
  ```
  $ git clone https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_ID/Kitura
  ```
  - If you’re on macOS, Xcode can help a lot. Generate an Xcode project with:
    ```
    $ swift package generate-xcodeproj
    ```
    Then open it:
    ```
    $ open *.xcodeproj
    ```
  *Note: Linux users, you’ll need a different editor.*

- **Apache License header:** Copy it from this Github Gist and paste it at the top of new files. Mandatory for all submitted code.

- Make sure all tests pass with:
  ```
  $ swift test
  ```
  Add new tests if you add new functionality. Need help? Slack us.

- **Pull Requests (PRs):** Run `swift test` again before you make a PR. Travis CI will check it’s cross-platform compatible (macOS + Linux).

- To open a PR:
  - Go to your repo fork.
  - Click "New pull request".
  - Ensure "base" is `master` and "compare" is your branch.
  - Click the green "Create pull request" button.

- If it’s your first PR, a bot will link you to sign a CLA. Do it ASAP.

- PR Guidelines:
  - Keep changes minimal and don't reformat code unless you open a separate PR for that.
  - Use `git diff --check` to avoid unnecessary white space issues.
  - Stick to the coding standards!

- **Coding Style:** Follow the Kitura Coding Standards, which are loosely based on GitHub's Swift Style Guide. Keep Swift Lint happy. 🤓

- **CLA:** Sign it if you want your changes merged. That's a must!

- Slack is our main chat. Use it for Qs or help. 🤙

Phew, that's the gist. Good luck!

Hey there! So you wanna contribute to LinearMouse? Nice! First off, check out the Code of Conduct. It's super important for keeping things respectful.

You'll need:
- Xcode (make sure it's got Swift 6.0 or newer)
- SwiftLint (for linting Swift files)
- SwiftFormat (for formatting Swift files)
- npm & ts-json-schema-generator (for that JSON schema gen)

Use brew to install all this stuff:

```
brew install swiftlint swiftformat npm
```

Once you've got that, set up the repo. Then, you gotta deal with code signing 'cause Apple loves that. Run this:

```
make configure
```

Don't touch the 'Signing & Capabilities' in Xcode directly! Use `make configure` or tweak `Signing.xcconfig`. 🚫❌

If you don't have certs in your Keychain, it'll just use ad-hoc ones. But, you might have to re-grant accessibility perms after rebuilding. So, consider getting an Apple Development cert in Xcode—it's free! 🆓

Alright, once you're all set, you can actually build and package LinearMouse. Just run the build command and you're good to go! 🏃‍♂️💨

Hey new guy, here's the rundown on contribs for Applite. It's gonna be a bit of a mess since I'm just jotting this down as I go:

- **Goal**: Applite is trying to make Homebrew more accessible to non-terminal users. So it's an app store for third-party apps that hides all the techy bits. It has some features for experts, but they're not in the main UI. Keep that in mind.

- **Reporting a Bug**:
  - **Output**: If there's an error label on the app card, click the terminal icon next to it and paste that output into the issue. It's super useful.
  - **Console.app**: For other issues, use Console.app.
    1. Choose your device.
    2. Start streaming.
    3. Reproduce the issue, then pause.
    4. Filter for `dev.aerolite.Applite` or search for "applite".
    5. Copy the log entries around the failure. If stuff is blank, check out this Stack Exchange answer: [link here].

- **Feature Requests**:
  - Open an issue or a discussion. Describe what you're missing and why. Try not to suggest anything that's only useful to someone who already knows Homebrew.

- **Contributing Code**:
  - Small fixes? Just PR them. For bigger stuff, talk first on Discord or open an issue.
  - **Building**: Use Xcode 16 or newer. Open `Applite.xcodeproj` and build. SwiftPM takes care of the dependencies.
  - **Project Layout**: Xcode 16 file-system synced groups mean the disk structure is the project structure. Just move files around on disk and Xcode picks it up.
  - **Conventions**: 
    - Use `@Observable` and `@MainActor`, no Combine.
    - Cask ID is `full_token` (tap/token). Bare tokens aren't unique.
    - Never block the UI on the brew CLI. Use SQLite first, then update reactively.
    - One view struct per file.

- **Translation Contributions**: Same as with any other contribution, but obviously, you'd be translating stuff.

- **AI-assisted Contributions**: Check out the CLAUDE.md at the repo root for project architecture if you're doing bigger changes.

Yeah, that's the gist. Good luck! Don't forget to check against the project goal first.

eqMac is totally getting a huge rewrite rn & it's kinda chaos trying to add big features. But hey, if you got ideas, hit GitHub first (make sure ur issue ain't already in the queue) or jump into Discord for a chat. When u got the green light, do this:

- Fork
- Build
- Debug
- Fix
- Merge
- PR (Pull Request) to get it in 🚀

For starting the debug process in Xcode, check the docs they mentioned.

---

If u wanna tackle the web UI locally, here's the play:

- Install Node.js LTS via NVM (Node Version Manager).
- Get Yarn v1 globally: `npm i -g yarn` (needed coz of Yarn Workspaces).

Then:

1. `yarn` in the root of the Monorepo.
2. `cd ui/`
3. `yarn start` to kick off the dev server.

---

For the native app + driver:

- Get Xcode.
- Install CocoaPods: `sudo gem install cocoapods`.

Then:

1. `cd native/`
2. `pod install`
3. `open eqMac.xcworkspace`
4. Run the **App - Debug** Scheme to launch eqMac in debug mode.

> P.S. Make sure ur environment is clean & updated before diving in. #justsaying

Hey there! 🚀 So, yea, SwiftyStoreKit is getting super popular and the main guy can't keep up. So, they're opening up the community to help out. 🤝

- Look for issues with the blue "contributions welcome" label. 🚪
- Start small, the maintainer will throw u some easy tasks if ur new.
- Once u get the hang of it, u can handle harder stuff and maybe even get admin rights. 🛡️

Quick note: Issues and PRs might not get looked at right away. So be patient, ok? 🕒

### Scope

- SwiftyStoreKit is a lightweight wrapper around StoreKit. 🤔
- It doesn't keep IAP data locally. U gotta use ur own storage thing (NSUserDefaults, CoreData, Keychain).
- Swift 2.3 and 2.2 branches are deprecated. 📉
- We're on Swift 3.x and 4.x now. 🚀
- Can't use it in Objective-C projects yet. 🚫

### Pull Requests
- Use gitflow model.
- New features and bug fixes go into `develop`. 🌱
- Hot fixes can go into both `master` and `develop`. 🔥
- Maintainer will merge `develop` into `master` and tag releases. 🏷️

### Open Features / Enhancements
- Local receipt validation. 📝
- Support for Apple-hosted content (non-consumable). 🎁
- Want more unit tests? 🧪
  - DI for SwiftyStoreKit
  - Tests for main class
  - Tests for receipt verification

### Issues
- Before opening a new issue, check if it's already there. 👀

Hope this helps! Good luck! 😄

Hey buddy,

So you wanna contribute to DigUp? Cool, but first things first:

- **Open an issue first**: Don't write any code until you've opened an issue. Someone might be working on it already. Saves time & frustration. PRs without an issue get closed. 🙅

- **Pull requests**: Once you're green lighted:
  - Just one fix or feature per PR, with a clear reason.
  - `swift test` must pass. Also `cargo test` in `shell/src-tauri` if you touch the Windows/Linux app. 📝
  - If it changes search results, run evals in `evals/` and include the results. (Check "Build from source" in the README).
  - Measure speed or memory changes before/after on the same machine.
  - **Don't send data elsewhere**: No telemetry or cloud stuff here.

- **Where everything is**:
  - Search engine in `Sources/DigUpKit`; same Swift code across all systems. System-specific stuff is in `Platform/Apple` and `Platform/Portable`.
  - Mac app in `Sources/DigUpApp` (SwiftUI); Windows/Linux in `shell/` (Tauri: Rust, HTML/JS).
  - `scripts/` builds llama.cpp, ffmpeg, etc. `.github/workflows/packages.yml` shows all the build steps.
  - "Build from source" in the README will help you get started.

- **Updating portable engine dependencies**:
  - `scripts/fetch-vendor.sh` checks SQLite, miniz, PDFium, stb against SHA-256 pins in `scripts/vendor-checksums.json`.
  - Update hashes when changing versions. Use verified checksums, not from untrusted sources.
  - Changing pins invalidates the vendor cache.

- **What to expect**:
  - DigUp is a side project, so replies can take a few days. No response means busy, not ignored.
  - Not every PR gets merged, even if it's good. It might not fit the project's direction.

- **Reporting a bug**: Make it useful:
  - Include your computer details (chip, memory, processor, graphics card), system & DigUp versions.
  - Describe what you did and what you expected.
  - Logs are in:
    - Mac: `~/Library/Application Support/DigUp/index.noindex` (`app.log`, `indexer.log`).
    - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\com.abdurrahim.DigUp\logs` and `worker.log` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DigUp\index`.
    - Linux: `~/.local/share/com.abdurrahim.DigUp/logs` and `worker.log` in `~/.local/share/digup/index`.
  - Look through logs before pasting. They might have file names and searches. 🧐

- **Security issues**: Use "Report a vulnerability" on the Security tab, not a public issue.

Hope this helps, and good luck! 🍀
